trigger.snippet: | `melian doctor` | Checks Node, git and `--attr-source`, Pi's login, providers with credentials, the GitHub token's source, gh, and the repository. It names which `melian` ran and warns when it lies inside the checkout. The `clone` line names the linked git clone, its commit, and whether its tree is clean. It warns when the clone is dirty or git cannot read it. An install under `node_modules` omits that line. Doctor also checks the state directory and whether it is writable. Its `evidence` line names the evidence directory, its size and `evidence.budget`, and warns once the directory has reached the budget, since a valid miss then keeps no more until `evidence.budget` is raised in the configuration; `melian store prune` keeps evidence until [issue #627](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/627) lands. Its `records` line, when the checkout has an `origin`, fetches the `melian/state` branch's tip into the store's own repository. It names, as a warning, up to five files on it that Melian did not write, which refuse calls until a writer removes them, or warns that the branch cannot be read. Opening the store sweeps what killed calls left in the state directory, and the line warns about what that sweep left: up to five leftovers it kept because it cannot tell their maker is gone, up to five of an exited call it could not remove, how many stale ones it ran out of time to remove, or left because it could not list every leftover, which the next open removes, that it stopped listing at its bound of 1,000 leftovers, and a process table it could not read, which sweeps nothing and keeps every leftover it found. It names them after the branch's own warning when the branch cannot be read, since the sweep ran when the store opened. A sweep that removed all it found says nothing. The same line then says whom the committed root policy trusts to write the branch. It reads `trust.writers` from the same base as the `trust` line. With it on, the line says the branch's writers are trusted as the repository's writers. With it off, it warns that only the trusted host may write `melian/state`, since doctor cannot check who may push to it. When no policy can be read, it warns that who may write the branch is unknown. A policy read from local `main` or `HEAD` makes the line a warning, with the `trust` line's caveat. Doctor reads the cached remote-tracking ref and never fetches it. So a clone that has not fetched reports the policy as of its last fetch, and each of the two lines names the ref and commit it read. [Issue #491](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/491) would check that commit against the remote. It never pushes and never fails. It also checks the named credentials of the secrets files, failing when git tracks `melian.local.yaml` or `melian.secrets.yaml` or a secrets file cannot be read, and warning for one others can read. It checks whether each lens's levels cost more from `quick` to `deep`, warning for a level on a lighter tier or with a smaller token or tool budget than the level below it. Its `resolution` lines list, for each `melian.yaml` and preference file in the working tree, every farther value and lens default its `resolution` overrides, or say that none does. It checks whether Biome and tsc come from the checkout or Melian's own copy. Its `probes` line runs an empty probe and says whether probes run here, or why every probe is refused, as a warning. Each manifest tool has a readiness line: materialised and verified, not yet fetched, unavailable, or manifest mismatch. `unavailable` marks a platform with no pin or a cache path that cannot be inspected, and doctor reports it as a warning. Doctor never downloads or runs a manifest tool; a mismatch fails doctor. Its standards line counts regular standards files and their bytes at every depth, warns for oversized files and skipped symlinks, and lists at most ten paths. Its `decision index` line gives the size of the decision index at `HEAD`, and warns past 64 KiB, with the warning `melian review` gives, or when the decisions cannot be read; it never fails. Its `routes` line names each tier’s resolved provider/model route and status, including the verifier. It also prints the review plan it would resolve now, as `plan` lines. Each routed tier shows its models, the credential each comes from, and the file that routed it, or that it was derived. Each lens's levels show the tier and model of each, and a lens with its own route has a `route` line and shows each level on the lens route. Every warning appears too. A tier with no route names the lenses that use it and the ways to fix it. Other warnings name missing credentials, a tier policy refuses, a route off the committed one, or a route model the catalogue does not hold, with the file that set it and, for an unknown provider, the provider. It fails with its own `decisions` line when `melian.yaml` sets `decisions.provider` | `0`, or `1` when Node or git cannot run a review, `melian.yaml` sets `decisions.provider`, git tracks a file only a maintainer may hold, a secrets file cannot be read, or a named credential's provider is unknown or accepts neither API keys nor OAuth tokens, or a manifest tool mismatches its pin |

snippet.text: Problem: a valid miss is judged against a round, and the conversations that missed it live only in the round's telemetry, which a later review of the same head does not reproduce. Example: a rerun on a host gives the lenses a new conversation, so the question "did the lens see these lines" can no longer be asked of the run that missed them. Solution: when `melian compare adjudicate` marks an external finding `valid` and no match names it, Melian copies the round's covering lens conversations and the verifier conversations that judged a sighting on the miss's lines to `<state>/evidence/<changeset>/<round>/`, one gzipped file per stage under `stages/`, written once however many misses share it, and a pointer under `misses/<external>.json` naming the base, head and policy commits and the lens files' blob IDs. Each stage keeps its leading entries, the prompt and the lens's instructions before the first reply, and as many of its last entries as fit in 16 MiB, and records how many it dropped; leading entries that alone pass 16 MiB keep as many from the first as fit. The directory holds the head's code and tool output, so it is never shared, exported or posted: only `melian compare evidence` reads it, and it prints through visible text. It is durable, and `evidence.budget`, 1 GiB by default, bounds it: a write past the budget is refused, writing no file and losing no evidence, the adjudication still recorded, and the refusal says to raise `evidence.budget` until [issue #627](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/627) builds the prune. A round whose run this clone holds no telemetry for, such as an Actions round, keeps nothing and says so. [The evidence decision](decisions/2026-11-20-miss-evidence-is-kept.md) records the rules.

snippet.text: | `melian store prune [--apply]` | Plans what [the retention decision](../decisions/2026-11-14-store-retention.md) lets Melian remove from the clone's state directory, found as storage is, and prints each entry with its size, a count and size per kind, the space it frees, the changeset files it keeps, the size of `evidence/`, and every name it does not recognise. It removes nothing without `--apply`. It never removes a changeset file, its `-wal` or `-shm`, `evidence/`, `scripted/`, or an unrecognised name. A live static check, a worktree locked by `melian-static pid <pid>` whose process is alive, stops it before it removes anything and is named on standard error. A state directory that is itself a link is refused, naming it, since prune does not follow a linked state directory | `0`, `1` when a static check is running, the state directory is a link, or the state directory or git cannot be read, `64` for anything after `prune` or `--apply` on another command |
